archetype.name: Gunslinger (reined in)
archetype.definition: A long-time aggressive, play-extending passer who is being asked this year to manage games behind a top-two defense and a run-first plan, and whose risk-taking now shows up as sacks more than interceptions.

report.headline: A muzzled gunslinger whose sacks and third downs are sinking a run-first offense
report.take:
Mayfield's track record says he is a volume thrower who lives with mistakes. In 2024 he threw 41 touchdowns, second in the league, at 0.207 EPA a play. Last year he was still a solid starter at 0.089, 26th. This season he sits at -0.248 EPA per dropback, 42nd of 47, over five starts split by a three-week stretch in which Jalon Daniels started (weeks 4-6). The team around him has changed shape. Tampa's defense ranks 2nd in EPA and its run game 7th, and the offense passes 7 points less often than the situation predicts (28th). Since he returned, the Bucs have won twice while he threw 11 passes and then 3. Right now he is the quarterback of a team that would prefer not to need one.

The damage has a specific shape. His dropbacks add up to -31.4 EPA, and third downs alone account for -19.5 of it: 29.3% conversions with an average of 8.3 yards to go and 7 sacks. Split by score, nearly all the harm comes in one-score games, at -0.468 EPA a play. The sack rate is 11.3% against a league average of 6.9%. When pressured he goes down 41.9% of the time, 37th of 38. Week 3 against Minnesota, now the league's top defense, was the low point: blitzed 26 times, sacked 6, bad throws on 30.3% of attempts. Week 1 was lost in a different way, with three fumbles lost in a six-point defeat.

The completion numbers hide where the value actually sits. His CPOE of +1.26 (21st) looks fine, but much of it comes from a Week 1 checkdown game: 4.7 intended air yards and +14 CPOE that still produced -5.4 EPA. Throws behind the line are completed 88% of the time and still lose 0.29 EPA a play, so the screen game is dead weight. The throws with value are the ones down the field. Intermediate passes run +0.173 EPA, middle-of-the-field throws +0.212, and his 10-plus air-yard attempts are positive while the under-10 group is negative. The deep ball has not landed, with 20% completions on 15 attempts. His best split, +0.288 EPA when trailing by 9 or more, is a 25-play garbage-time sample.

The sacks are not new. His pressure-to-sack rate has climbed for three straight years (0.357, 0.364, 0.391), and his time to throw is up to 2.99. That part of the problem is him, not noise. The fumble count and the third-down collapse should cool somewhat. Even so, losing Emeka Egbuka and facing a pass rush that ranks 2nd in sack rate make a clean rebound in Chicago unlikely.

strengths.title: Value lives in the intermediate middle
strengths.body: His throws in the 10-19 yard window and over the middle are the only parts of his passing tree adding positive EPA. That fits who he has been: a passer who wins when he lets it rip into tight windows rather than living on the perimeter. The samples are small (27 and 20 attempts), but this is the version of him that produced 2023-24. It is the area to lean on if Tampa ever opens the offense up.

strengths.title: Legs still bail out broken plays
strengths.body: Scrambles have returned +0.187 EPA each with four first downs, and his few designed runs have been positive too. He has run for 382 and 378 yards the last two seasons, top ten both years, so this is a stable skill. It is the one way he currently turns pressure into something useful instead of a sack.

strengths.title: Comfortable when the game opens up
strengths.body: When trailing by 9 or more he has completed 87% of his passes at +0.288 EPA a play. Defenses play softer in that state, and with 25 plays this is a hint rather than a fact. It still matters this week: as a 6-point underdog against a top-ten offense, he may get more of those snaps.

concerns.title: Holding the ball into sacks
concerns.body: An 11.3% sack rate (42nd) and a 41.9% pressure-to-sack rate (37th of 38) are the biggest single drag on his line. This is a real flaw rather than a byproduct of scrambling: the scrambles help, but nowhere near enough to pay for the sacks. His pressure-to-sack rate has risen three years running, and his time to throw is up again this year. Expect it to persist, especially against good rushes.

concerns.title: Third-and-long is a black hole
concerns.body: Third downs have cost -19.5 EPA with a 29.3% conversion rate. The setup is bad: an average of 8.3 yards to go, created by a run-first early-down plan and negative screens. He then makes it worse with seven third-down sacks. The sacks are a skill issue that will stay. The extreme conversion rate on 41 plays should drift up somewhat.

concerns.title: Ball security and dead screens
concerns.body: Three lost fumbles rank 43rd of 47, all in Week 1. He has also put the ball on the ground six times in turnover-worthy fashion, which ties back to the sacks. The fumble recovery luck will even out, but the handling is a pattern worth tracking. Separately, his behind-the-line throws complete 88% of the time and still lose EPA. Bucky Irving's targets are negative per play, so the easy completions are not moving the chains.

trend.note: His volume has shrunk from 34 attempts in Weeks 2-3 to 11 and then 3 since his return, as Tampa wins on defense and the run. Over his last three games his CPOE is 7.9 points below his season mark. Per-dropback EPA is slightly better lately, but it rests on very few throws.

nextGame.headline: Sack-prone passer meets the league's second-best sack defense
nextGame.body:
Chicago is a mixed matchup for him. The Bears sack quarterbacks at the 2nd-highest rate and are 4th against short passes, which attacks exactly the parts of his game that are broken: holding the ball, and checkdowns that go nowhere. They are also the worst defense in the league on deep throws and 22nd in explosive pass rate, and they allow 19.1 PPR a game to quarterbacks (25th). As 6-point road underdogs against a Bears offense ranked 8th, the Bucs are likely to throw more than their usual run-first plan allows. That raises his volume floor, but the efficiency risk stays.

Availability cuts both ways. Emeka Egbuka, his most-targeted receiver at 86% of snaps, is out with a foot injury, so the passing game narrows to Chris Godwin Jr., his most efficient target, plus Cade Otton and the struggling Ted Hurst III. On Chicago's side, CB Malik Muhammad II (toe) and DE Grady Jarrett (groin) were both hurt in the Seahawks game, and their status for Sunday is uncertain. Muhammad's absence would help the outside throws. Jarrett missing would take some heat off a pass rush he cannot afford to face at full strength.

keyMatchups.title: Bears pass rush versus his clock
keyMatchups.body: Chicago's sack rate ranks 2nd, and his pressure-to-sack rate is 37th of 38. If Jarrett plays, expect drives to stall on third-and-long the way they did against Minnesota. Getting the ball out on time is the whole game for him.

keyMatchups.title: A leaky deep defense he can't hit
keyMatchups.body: Chicago gives up the most EPA in the league on deep passes. His own deep ball has connected on just 20% of 15 attempts. Whether he can finally hit a couple of shots, likely to Godwin, decides whether the volume becomes production.

keyMatchups.title: Otton up the seam
keyMatchups.body: The Bears rank 28th in EPA allowed to lead tight ends. With Egbuka out, Otton's middle-of-the-field targets line up with the only area where Mayfield is adding value.

nextGame.watch: His third-and-long dropbacks: whether he throws into the intermediate middle or takes the sack.

restOfSeason.body:
Tampa's structure is not changing. A top-two defense and a top-ten run game mean the Bucs will keep limiting his dropbacks when they lead, so expect something like 140-200 passing yards a game rather than last year's 217. The sack problem is multi-year and should keep his sack rate well above the league norm. The parts likely to improve are the three-fumble Week 1, the extreme third-down conversion rate, and some of the failed screen game, which together should move his per-dropback EPA closer to average. A return to 2024's level is unlikely.

The fantasy and efficiency upside comes from game script. In games where Tampa trails, he has looked like his old self on a small sample, so his best weeks will likely be losses. Egbuka's return and Godwin's health matter most for whether the downfield throws he still makes can carry the offense.
swingFactors: Egbuka's return from the foot injury
How often Tampa trails and has to throw
Whether his sack rate comes down from 11%

confidence.note: Only five starts, two of them nearly without passes, split by a three-week absence in a run-first offense.
